- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

  title: OpenAPI
  description: Tally's API
  license:
    name: MIT
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.tally.so
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
paths:
  /forms:
    post:
      summary: Create a new form
      description: >-
        Creates a new form, optionally based on a template or within a specific
        workspace.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                workspaceId:
                  type: string
                  description: >-
                    ID of the workspace to create the form in. If not provided,
                    uses the user's default workspace
                templateId:
                  type: string
                  description: ID of the template to base the form on
                folderId:
                  type: string
                  description: >-
                    ID of the folder to place the form in. Must belong to the
                    target workspace.
                status:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/FormStatus'
                  description: Initial status of the form
                blocks:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/Block'
                settings:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/FormSettings'
              required:
                - blocks
                - status
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Form created successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Form'
        '400':
          description: Invalid request body
        '401':
          description: Unauthorized
      security:
        - bearerAuth: []
components:
  schemas:
    FormStatus:
      type: string
      enum:
        - BLANK
        - DRAFT
        - PUBLISHED
      description: >-
        Deleting a form is done through DELETE /forms/{formId}, which moves it
        to the trash so it can be restored.
    Block:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/FormTitleBlock'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/TitleBlock'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/TextBlock'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/LabelBlock'

import re

# print each schema block for choice-related types + payloads + BlockUuid/GroupUuid
for name in ['MultipleChoiceOptionBlock','CheckboxBlock','DropdownOptionBlock','BlockUuid','GroupUuid']:
    m=re.search(rf'    {name}:\n(?:      .*\n|\n)*?(?=    [A-Z][A-Za-z]+:\n|$)', src)
    if m:
        print('='*20, name, '='*20)
        print(m.group(0)[:1800])
EOF

Here's what the search turned up for creating Tally.so forms with `MULTIPLE_CHOICE_OPTION` blocks:

## Key Resources Found

1. **[Tally API Reference – POST /forms](https://developers.tally.so/api-reference/endpoint/forms/post)** — The official endpoint spec (`POST https://api.tally.so/forms`, Bearer auth). It defines the `MultipleChoiceOptionBlock` schema with required fields: `uuid`, `type`, `groupUuid`, `groupType`, and `payload`.

2. **[Blocks Reference – Multiple choice option](https://developers.tally.so/blocks-reference/multiple-choice-option)** — Dedicated docs page for this block type.

3. **[GitHub SKILL.md example](https://github.com/openclaw/skills/blob/main/skills/yujesyoga/tally/SKILL.md)** — Contains working JSON examples.

## Schema Highlights

Per the official API spec, each option block requires:
- `uuid` (unique), `type: MULTIPLE_CHOICE_OPTION`
- `groupUuid` shared across the question, `groupType: MULTIPLE_CHOICE`
- Payload requires: `index`, `isFirst`, `isLast`

Optional payload fields include `text`, `isRequired`, `allowMultiple`, `hasOtherOption`/`isOtherOption`, `randomize`, `badgeType` (`OFF`/`NUMBERS`/`LETTERS`), and `color`.

## Working JSON Example (from the GitHub result)

A multiple-choice question consists of a TITLE block plus one option block per answer:

```json
{
  "uuid": "q2-title",
  "type": "TITLE",
  "groupUuid": "group-q2",
  "groupType": "QUESTION",
  "payload": {
    "safeHTMLSchema": [["How did you hear about us?", [["tag", "span"]]]]
  }
},
{
  "uuid": "q2-opt1",
  "type": "MULTIPLE_CHOICE_OPTION",
  "groupUuid": "group-q2",
  "groupType": "MULTIPLE_CHOICE",
  "payload": { "isRequired": true, "index": 0, "isFirst": true, "isLast": false, "text": "Social media" }
},
{
  "uuid": "q2-opt2",
  "type": "MULTIPLE_CHOICE_OPTION",
  "groupUuid": "group-q2",
  "groupType": "MULTIPLE_CHOICE",
  "payload": { "isRequired": true, "index": 1, "isFirst": false, "isLast": true, "text": "Friend referral" }
}
```

**Notes:** Options are linked to their question via the shared `groupUuid`; `index` is zero-based; only the first option needs group-level settings like `randomize` or `hasBadge`. The same pattern applies to sibling types like `CHECKBOX` (groupType `CHECKBOXES`) and `DROPDOWN_OPTION` (groupType `DROPDOWN`). The PATCH `/forms` endpoint uses the identical block schema for updating.

Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
}

model Project {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  title           String

  problem         String   @default("")
  solution        String   @default("")

  category        String

  liveUrl         String?

  order           Int      @default(0)

  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  description String   @default("")
  ideal       String   @default("")
  features    String
  cta         String   @default("Get Started")
  highlighted Boolean  @default(false)
  order       Int      @default(0)
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
}

model ServiceAddon {
  id    String @id @default(cuid())
  name  String
  price String
  order Int    @default(0)
}

model FAQ {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  question  String
  answer    String
  section   String   @default("general")
  order     Int      @default(0)
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model Essay {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  title         String
  slug          String    @unique
  body          String
  excerpt       String?
  tags          String?
  coverImageId  String?
  coverImageUrl String?
  status        String    @default("draft")
  publishedAt   DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
}

model ICApplication {

  building       String
  challenge      String

  value     String

  key       String   @unique
  value     String

import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
import { PrismaLibSql } from '@prisma/adapter-libsql'
import { projects } from '../data/projects'
import { galleryPhotos } from '../data/gallery'
import { socialData } from '../data/social'

const adapter = new PrismaLibSql({
  url: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'file:./prisma/dev.db',
  authToken: process.env.DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN,
})
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter })

async function main() {
  await prisma.project.deleteMany()
  await prisma.testimonial.deleteMany()
  await prisma.serviceTier.deleteMany()
  await prisma.serviceAddon.deleteMany()
  await prisma.fAQ.deleteMany()
  await prisma.siteStat.deleteMany()
  await prisma.nowPage.deleteMany()
  await prisma.siteSettings.deleteMany()
  await prisma.galleryImage.deleteMany()
  await prisma.aboutPage.deleteMany()
  await prisma.experienceEntry.deleteMany()

  await prisma.project.createMany({
    data: projects.map((p, i) => ({
      title: p.title,
      description: p.description,
      longDescription: p.longDescription,
      problem: p.problem,
      solution: p.solution,
      myRole: p.myRole,
      status: p.status,
      statusLabel: p.statusLabel,
      category: p.category,
      techStack: JSON.stringify(p.tech),
      liveUrl: p.live ?? null,
      githubUrl: p.github ?? null,
      imageUrl: p.image ?? null,
      featured: p.featured,
      order: i,
    })),
  })

  const testimonials = [
    {
      quote:
        "Kennedy doesn't just build websites — he builds systems. The Breeze Aircons platform he delivered changed how we operate entirely.",
      authorName: 'Client — Breeze Aircons Ltd',
      authorRole: 'Business Owner · Nairobi, Kenya',
      authorCompany: 'Breeze Aircons Ltd',
      projectRef: 'Breeze Aircons',
    },
    {
      quote:
        'Working with Kennedy on the Royal Priesthood app was a seamless experience. He understood the ministry context immediately.',
      authorName: 'Royal Priesthood Ministry',
      authorRole: "Leadership Team · Murang'a, Kenya",
    },
    {
      quote:
        'He thinks in systems, not just features. Kennedy asks "why" before he writes a single line.',
      authorName: 'Tech Collaborator',
      authorRole: 'Fellow Developer · Nairobi, Kenya',
    },
    {
      quote:
        'Kennedy delivered our project on time, on budget, and above spec.',
      authorName: 'Startup Founder',
      authorRole: 'Founder · Nairobi Tech Scene',
    },
  ]

  await prisma.testimonial.createMany({
    data: testimonials.map((t, i) => ({ ...t, order: i })),
  })

  const tiers = [
    {
      name: 'Digital Presence',
      label: 'Starter',
      priceRange: 'KES 10,000 – 25,000',
      usd: '~$75 – $190',
      delivery: '7-day delivery',
      description: 'A clean, professional web presence that makes you look legit from day one.',
      ideal: 'Solopreneurs, small businesses, personal brands',
      features: JSON.stringify([
        'Landing page or portfolio site',
        'Tailwind CSS + Next.js — fast, modern',
        'Mobile-first responsive design',
        'Deployed to Vercel with custom domain setup',
        '1 revision round',
      ]),
      cta: 'Start a Project',
      highlighted: false,
      order: 0,
    },
    {
      name: 'Full-Stack Build',
      label: 'Growth',
      priceRange: 'KES 35,000 – 80,000',
      usd: '~$265 – $610',
      delivery: '2–3 week delivery',
      description: 'A real product with a real backend — auth, database, payments, admin panel.',
      ideal: 'Startups needing a working MVP',
      features: JSON.stringify([
        'Multi-page web application',
        'Supabase backend (database + auth)',
        'M-Pesa / payment integration',
        'Admin panel for content management',
        '2 revision rounds + 1-week support',
      ]),
      cta: 'Build with Me',
      highlighted: true,
      order: 1,
    },
    {
      name: 'Product Co-Build',
      label: 'Scale',
      priceRange: 'KES 100,000 – 250,000',
      usd: '~$760 – $1,900',
      delivery: '4–6 week delivery',
      description: 'Full SaaS or platform build from PRD to production with ongoing support.',
      ideal: 'Founders building for a real user base',
      features: JSON.stringify([
        'PRD + architecture design + development',
        'Full SaaS or platform infrastructure',
        'Multi-tenant, role-based access control',
        'Deployment + CI/CD pipeline setup',
        '1 month post-launch support',
      ]),
      cta: "Let's Co-Build",
      highlighted: false,
      order: 2,
    },
  ]

  await prisma.serviceTier.createMany({ data: tiers })

  await prisma.serviceAddon.createMany({
    data: [
      { name: 'UI/UX Design', price: '+KES 5,000', order: 0 },
      { name: 'Brand Identity', price: '+KES 8,000', order: 1 },
      { name: 'M-Pesa Integration', price: '+KES 6,000', order: 2 },
      { name: 'WhatsApp Bot Integration', price: '+KES 7,000', order: 3 },
    ],
  })

  const faqs = [
    {
      question: 'Do you work with clients outside Kenya?',
      answer:
        'Yes. I work with founders and businesses globally. Payment can be made via M-Pesa, bank transfer, or international payment links.',
      section: 'general',
      order: 0,
    },
    {
      question: 'What do you need from me to start?',
      answer:
        "A clear brief on what you need, your brand assets if available, and a budget range. Book a free 30-min call and we'll map it out.",
      section: 'general',
      order: 1,
    },
    {
      question: 'How long does a typical project take?',
      answer:
        'Starter projects: 7 days. Growth builds: 2–3 weeks. Scale/SaaS builds: 4–6 weeks.',
      section: 'general',
      order: 2,
    },
    {
      question: 'Who can join the Inner Circle?',
      answer:
        'Builders actively shipping work — founders, developers, creatives, and technologists who want accountability and peer support.',
      section: 'community',
      order: 0,
    },
    {
      question: 'Is the Inner Circle free?',
      answer: 'Yes. Access is application-only and curated, but there is no membership fee.',
      section: 'community',
      order: 1,
    },
  ]

  await prisma.fAQ.createMany({ data: faqs })

  await prisma.siteStat.createMany({
    data: [
      { key: 'active_builds', value: '3', label: 'Active Builds' },
      { key: 'projects_shipped', value: '5+', label: 'Projects Shipped' },
      { key: 'years_building', value: '3+', label: 'Years Building' },
      { key: 'community_members', value: '127', label: 'Community Members' },
      { key: 'clients_served', value: '10+', label: 'Clients Served' },
    ],
  })

  await prisma.nowPage.create({
    data: {
      building: JSON.stringify(['ADDPlus+', 'Caspahub', 'Portfolio v3.0 rebuild']),
      learning: JSON.stringify(['Systems design', 'Turso edge databases', 'Product storytelling']),
      reading: JSON.stringify(['The Mom Test', 'Building Microservices']),
      thisWeeksWin: 'Shipped portfolio v3.0 foundation with Turso + admin dashboard.',
    },
  })

  await prisma.galleryImage.createMany({
    data: galleryPhotos.map((p, i) => ({
      imageId: p.src.replace(/^\/gallery\//, '').replace(/\.[^.]+$/, ''),
      imageUrl: p.src,
      caption: p.caption,
      category: p.category,
      location: p.location ?? null,
      date: p.date ?? null,
      visible: true,
      order: i,
    })),
  })

  await prisma.siteSettings.createMany({
    data: [
      {
        key: 'ic_tagline',
        value: 'A community for builders who move with intention.',
      },
      {
        key: 'ic_quote',
        value:
          'Not a mailing list. Not a Discord full of noise. A curated space for builders shipping real work.',
      },
      {
        key: 'social_data',
        value: JSON.stringify(socialData),
      },
    ],
  })

  await prisma.aboutPage.create({
    data: {
      id: 'main',
      paragraphs: JSON.stringify([
        'My name is Kennedy and I build digital systems that serve people. I started building on the web in 2022 — what began as curiosity quickly became a calling.',
        "I operate at the intersection of **systems thinking**, **creative technology**, and **purposeful building**. I don't just write code — I architect solutions, from PRD to deployment, with a deep focus on the people who will use them.",
        "Currently pursuing **Mechatronics Engineering** at Murang'a University of Technology, building **ADDPlus+** (a marketplace for Kenya's informal economy) and **Caspahub** (an AI-native OS for car wash businesses), and taking on select freelance projects for founders who need a technical partner, not just a developer.",
        'I build with faith. I believe the work we do shapes the world we live in. *"To build is to serve."*',
        'Technologies I work with:',
      ]),
      skills: JSON.stringify([
        'TypeScript',
        'Next.js',
        'React Native',
        'Supabase',
        'PostgreSQL',
        'Node.js',
        'Tailwind CSS',
        'M-Pesa Daraja API',
      ]),
      profileImageUrl: '/images/profile.svg',
    },
  })

  const experiences = [
    {
      company: "Murang'a University",
      title: 'Mechatronics Engineering Student',
      period: '2023 — Present',
      url: 'https://www.mut.ac.ke',
      points: JSON.stringify([
        'Pursuing a degree in Mechatronics Engineering, combining mechanical, electrical, and software systems',
        'Developing skills in embedded systems, automation, IoT, and control systems',
        'Building projects that integrate hardware and software — from robotic systems to IoT platforms',
        'Applying engineering principles to digital product design and systems architecture',
      ]),
      order: 0,
    },
    {
      company: 'DirectEd Development',
      title: 'Scholar & Developer',
      period: '2022 — 2023',
      url: 'https://directed.dev',
      points: JSON.stringify([
        'Selected as a scholar in the DirectEd Development Foundation program for emerging tech talent in Africa',
        'Gained hands-on experience in web development, software engineering, and product thinking',
        'Built projects using modern web technologies including React, Node.js, and TypeScript',
        'Participated in mentorship programs with industry professionals across the UK and Africa',
      ]),
      order: 1,
    },
    {
      company: 'Freelance',
      title: 'Full-Stack Developer & Technical Partner',
      period: '2022 — Present',
      url: '#',
      points: JSON.stringify([
        'Design and build custom digital products for founders, startups, and small businesses across Kenya and globally',
        'Deliver end-to-end: from architecture and design to deployment and handover',
        'Specialise in Next.js, Supabase, M-Pesa integration, and mobile-first responsive systems',
        'Work as a technical co-founder partner for early-stage founders who need a builder, not just a developer',
      ]),
      order: 2,
    },
    {
      company: 'Founder',
      title: 'Building ADDPlus+ & Caspahub',
      period: '2025 — Present',
      url: '#',
      points: JSON.stringify([
        "Building ADDPlus+: a multi-vendor marketplace for Nairobi's informal economy with M-Pesa escrow",
        'Building Caspahub: an AI-native operating system for car wash businesses across East Africa',
        'Leading full product cycles — PRD, design, architecture, development, and go-to-market',
        "Applying systems thinking to build infrastructure that serves Kenya's informal economy",
      ]),
      order: 3,
    },
  ]

  await prisma.experienceEntry.createMany({ data: experiences })

  console.log('Seed complete')
}

main()
  .catch((e) => {
    console.error(e)
    process.exit(1)
  })
  .finally(async () => {
    await prisma.$disconnect()
  })

export type Role = 'admin' | 'editor'

export type Module =
  | 'dashboard'
  | 'coffees'
  | 'content'
  | 'business'
  | 'community'
  | 'hq'
  | 'integrations'
  | 'settings'

export type Action = 'read' | 'write'

const MATRIX: Record<Module, Partial<Record<Action, Role[]>>> = {
  dashboard: { read: ['admin', 'editor'] },
  coffees: { read: ['admin'], write: ['admin'] },
  content: { read: ['admin', 'editor'], write: ['admin', 'editor'] },
  business: { read: ['admin', 'editor'], write: ['admin', 'editor'] },
  community: { read: ['admin'], write: ['admin'] },
  hq: { read: ['admin'], write: ['admin'] },
  integrations: { read: ['admin'], write: ['admin'] },
  settings: { read: ['admin'], write: ['admin'] },
}

const ROUTE_MODULES: { prefix: string; module: Module }[] = [
  { prefix: '/admin/dashboard', module: 'dashboard' },
  { prefix: '/admin/coffees', module: 'coffees' },
  { prefix: '/admin/projects', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/essays', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/now', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/about', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/experience', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/gallery', module: 'content' },
  { prefix: '/admin/services', module: 'business' },
  { prefix: '/admin/testimonials', module: 'business' },
  { prefix: '/admin/faq', module: 'business' },
  { prefix: '/admin/stats', module: 'business' },
  { prefix: '/admin/community', module: 'community' },
  { prefix: '/admin/hq', module: 'hq' },
  { prefix: '/admin/integrations', module: 'integrations' },
  { prefix: '/admin/settings', module: 'settings' },
  { prefix: '/admin/studio', module: 'settings' },
]

export function can(role: string | undefined, module: Module, action: Action): boolean {
  if (!role) return false
  const allowed = MATRIX[module][action] ?? []
  return allowed.includes(role as Role)
}

export function moduleForPath(pathname: string): Module | null {
  const sorted = [...ROUTE_MODULES].sort((a, b) => b.prefix.length - a.prefix.length)
  for (const { prefix, module } of sorted) {
    if (pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`)) return module
  }
  return null
}

export function canAccessPath(role: string | undefined, pathname: string): boolean {
  if (pathname === '/admin' || pathname === '/admin/login') return true
  const mod = moduleForPath(pathname)
  if (!mod) return true
  return can(role, mod, 'read')
}

export function defaultPathForRole(role: Role): string {
  return role === 'editor' ? '/admin/projects' : '/admin/dashboard'
}

export type NavItem = {
  href: string
  label: string
  module: Module
}

export const NAV_ITEMS: NavItem[] = [
  { href: '/admin/dashboard', label: 'Dashboard', module: 'dashboard' },
  { href: '/admin/coffees', label: 'Payments', module: 'coffees' },
  { href: '/admin/projects', label: 'Projects', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/essays', label: 'Essays', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/now', label: 'Now Page', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/about', label: 'About', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/experience', label: 'Experience', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/gallery', label: 'Gallery', module: 'content' },
  { href: '/admin/services', label: 'Services', module: 'business' },
  { href: '/admin/testimonials', label: 'Testimonials', module: 'business' },
  { href: '/admin/faq', label: 'FAQs', module: 'business' },
  { href: '/admin/stats', label: 'Stats', module: 'business' },
  { href: '/admin/community', label: 'Community', module: 'community' },
  { href: '/admin/integrations', label: 'Integrations', module: 'integrations' },
  { href: '/admin/hq', label: 'Personal HQ', module: 'hq' },
  { href: '/admin/settings', label: 'Settings', module: 'settings' },
]

export const NAV_GROUPS: { title: string; moduleFilter: Module[] }[] = [
  { title: 'Overview', moduleFilter: ['dashboard', 'coffees'] },
  { title: 'Content', moduleFilter: ['content'] },
  { title: 'Business', moduleFilter: ['business'] },
  { title: 'Community', moduleFilter: ['community'] },
  { title: 'Integrations', moduleFilter: ['integrations', 'hq'] },
  { title: 'Settings', moduleFilter: ['settings'] },
]

function itemsForModules(modules: Module[]): NavItem[] {
  return NAV_ITEMS.filter((i) => modules.includes(i.module))
}

export function navGroupsForRole(role: string | undefined) {
  return NAV_GROUPS.map((group) => ({
    title: group.title,
    items: itemsForModules(group.moduleFilter).filter((item) => can(role, item.module, 'read')),
  })).filter((group) => group.items.length > 0)
}

1	import NextAuth from 'next-auth'
2	import Credentials from 'next-auth/providers/credentials'
3	import type { Role } from '@/lib/rbac'
4	
5	function resolveRole(password: string): Role | null {
6	  if (password === process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD) return 'admin'
7	  if (process.env.EDITOR_PASSWORD && password === process.env.EDITOR_PASSWORD) return 'editor'
8	  return null
9	}
10	
11	export const { handlers, signIn, signOut, auth } = NextAuth({
12	  providers: [
13	    Credentials({
14	      credentials: {
15	        password: { label: 'Password', type: 'password' },
16	      },
17	      authorize: async (credentials) => {
18	        const password = credentials?.password as string | undefined
19	        if (!password) return null
20	        const role = resolveRole(password)
21	        if (!role) return null
22	        return {
23	          id: role === 'admin' ? 'admin' : 'editor',
24	          name: role === 'admin' ? 'Kennedy Muritu' : 'Content Editor',
25	          role,
26	        }
27	      },
28	    }),
29	  ],
30	  callbacks: {
31	    jwt({ token, user }) {
32	      if (user?.role) token.role = user.role
33	      return token
34	    },
35	    session({ session, token }) {
36	      if (token.role) session.user.role = token.role as Role
37	      return session
38	    },
39	  },
40	  session: { strategy: 'jwt', maxAge: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 },
41	  pages: { signIn: '/admin/login' },
42	  trustHost: true,
43	})

1	import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
2	import { z } from 'zod'
3	import { prisma } from '@/lib/db'
4	import { initiateStkPush } from '@/lib/payhero'
5	import { createCoffeeReference } from '@/lib/payments/coffee-reference'
6	import { checkRateLimit } from '@/lib/rate-limit'
7	
8	const schema = z.object({
9	  phone: z.string().min(9).max(15),
10	  amountKes: z.number().int().min(50).max(5000),
11	  donorName: z.string().max(100).optional(),
12	  message: z.string().max(500).optional(),
13	})
14	
15	export async function POST(req: Request) {
16	  const ip = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',')[0]?.trim() ?? 'unknown'
17	  const allowed = await checkRateLimit(`coffee-api:${ip}`)
18	  if (!allowed) {
19	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Rate limit exceeded' }, { status: 429 })
20	  }
21	
22	  let body: unknown
23	  try {
24	    body = await req.json()
25	  } catch {
26	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid JSON' }, { status: 400 })
27	  }
28	
29	  const parsed = schema.safeParse(body)
30	  if (!parsed.success) {
31	    return NextResponse.json({ error: parsed.error.errors[0]?.message }, { status: 400 })
32	  }
33	
34	  const { phone, amountKes, donorName, message } = parsed.data
35	
36	  const donation = await prisma.coffeeDonation.create({
37	    data: {
38	      amountKes,
39	      phone,
40	      donorName: donorName ?? null,
41	      message: message ?? null,
42	      externalReference: 'pending',
43	      status: 'pending',
44	    },
45	  })
46	
47	  const externalReference = createCoffeeReference(donation.id)
48	  await prisma.coffeeDonation.update({
49	    where: { id: donation.id },
50	    data: { externalReference },
51	  })
52	
53	  const stk = await initiateStkPush({
54	    phone,
55	    amountKes,
56	    accountReference: externalReference,
57	    transactionDesc: 'Buy Kennedy a coffee',
58	    customerName: donorName,
59	  })
60	
61	  if (!stk.success) {
62	    await prisma.coffeeDonation.update({
63	      where: { id: donation.id },
64	      data: { status: 'failed' },
65	    })
66	    return NextResponse.json({ error: stk.message }, { status: 502 })
67	  }
68	
69	  if (stk.reference) {
70	    await prisma.coffeeDonation.update({
71	      where: { id: donation.id },
72	      data: { payheroReference: stk.reference },
73	    })
74	  }
75	
76	  return NextResponse.json({
77	    reference: externalReference,
78	    message: stk.message,
79	    simulated: stk.simulated ?? false,
80	  })

5	export type DayCount = { date: string; count: number; amount?: number }
6	
7	async function safeQuery<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, fallback: T): Promise<{ data: T; ok: boolean }> {
8	  try {
9	    return { data: await fn(), ok: true }
10	  } catch {
11	    return { data: fallback, ok: false }
12	  }
13	}
14	
15	function last7Days(): Date[] {
16	  const days: Date[] = []
17	  for (let i = 6; i >= 0; i--) {
18	    const d = new Date()
19	    d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)
20	    d.setDate(d.getDate() - i)
21	    days.push(d)
22	  }
23	  return days
24	}
25	
26	function dayKey(d: Date): string {
27	  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
28	}
29	
30	async function contactsByDay(): Promise<DayCount[]> {
31	  const since = new Date()
32	  since.setDate(since.getDate() - 6)
33	  since.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)
34	  const rows = await prisma.contactThread.findMany({
35	    where: { createdAt: { gte: since } },
36	    select: { createdAt: true },
37	  })
38	  const map = new Map<string, number>()
39	  for (const d of last7Days()) map.set(dayKey(d), 0)
40	  for (const r of rows) {
41	    const k = dayKey(new Date(r.createdAt))
42	    if (map.has(k)) map.set(k, (map.get(k) ?? 0) + 1)
43	  }
44	  return last7Days().map((d) => ({ date: dayKey(d), count: map.get(dayKey(d)) ?? 0 }))
45	}
46	
47	async function coffeeByDay(): Promise<DayCount[]> {
48	  const since = new Date()
49	  since.setDate(since.getDate() - 6)
50	  since.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)
51	  const rows = await prisma.coffeeDonation.findMany({
52	    where: { createdAt: { gte: since }, status: 'completed' },
53	    select: { createdAt: true, amountKes: true },
54	  })
55	  const countMap = new Map<string, number>()
56	  const amountMap = new Map<string, number>()
57	  for (const d of last7Days()) {
58	    const k = dayKey(d)
59	    countMap.set(k, 0)
60	    amountMap.set(k, 0)
61	  }
62	  for (const r of rows) {
63	    const k = dayKey(new Date(r.createdAt))
64	    if (countMap.has(k)) {
65	      countMap.set(k, (countMap.get(k) ?? 0) + 1)
66	      amountMap.set(k, (amountMap.get(k) ?? 0) + r.amountKes)
67	    }
68	  }
69	  return last7Days().map((d) => {
70	    const k = dayKey(d)
71	    return { date: k, count: countMap.get(k) ?? 0, amount: amountMap.get(k) ?? 0 }
72	  })
73	}
74	
75	export async function getDashboardData() {
76	  let degraded = false
77	
78	  const wrap = async <T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, fallback: T) => {
79	    const r = await safeQuery(fn, fallback)
80	    if (!r.ok) degraded = true
81	    return r.data
82	  }
83	
84	  const [
85	    projectCount,
86	    testimonialCount,
87	    publishedEssays,
88	    coffeeCount,
89	    coffeeTotalKes,
90	    contactCount,
91	    pendingCoffees,
92	    recentCoffees,
93	    recentContacts,
94	    recentEssays,
95	    coffeeTrend,
96	    contactTrend,
97	  ] = await Promise.all([
98	    wrap(() => prisma.project.count(), 0),
99	    wrap(() => prisma.testimonial.count(), 0),
100	    wrap(() => prisma.essay.count({ where: { status: 'published' } }), 0),
101	    wrap(() => prisma.coffeeDonation.count({ where: { status: 'completed' } }), 0),
102	    wrap(
103	      () =>
104	        prisma.coffeeDonation
105	          .aggregate({ where: { status: 'completed' }, _sum: { amountKes: true } })
106	          .then((r) => r._sum.amountKes ?? 0),
107	      0,
108	    ),
109	    wrap(() => prisma.contactThread.count(), 0),
110	    wrap(() => prisma.coffeeDonation.count({ where: { status: 'pending' } }), 0),
111	    wrap(
112	      () => prisma.coffeeDonation.findMany({ orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take: 5 }),
113	      [],
114	    ),
115	    wrap(
116	      () => prisma.contactThread.findMany({ orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take: 5 }),
117	      [],
118	    ),
119	    wrap(
120	      () => prisma.essay.findMany({ orderBy: { updatedAt: 'desc' }, take: 3 }),
121	      [],
122	    ),
123	    wrap(() => coffeeByDay(), []),
124	    wrap(() => contactsByDay(), []),
125	  ])
126	
127	  return {
128	    degraded,
129	    kpis: {
130	      projects: projectCount,
131	      coffeeTotalKes,
132	      conversations: contactCount,
133	      publishedEssays,
134	      testimonials: testimonialCount,
135	      coffeesReceived: coffeeCount,
136	      pendingCoffees,
137	    },
138	    recentCoffees,
139	    recentContacts,
140	    recentEssays,
141	    coffeeByDay: coffeeTrend,
142	    contactsByDay: contactTrend,
143	  }
144	}

from PIL import Image
import base64, io, os

os.makedirs('public/images', exist_ok=True)

def to_jpeg_datauri(im, quality=86, max_side=1100):
    if max(im.size) > max_side:
        im = im.resize((max_side, max_side), Image.LANCZOS)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(buf, 'JPEG', quality=quality, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
    return b64, len(buf.getvalue())

def wrap_svg(b64, w, h):
    return (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" '
            f'viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" width="{w}" height="{h}" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice">'
            f'<image width="{w}" height="{h}" xlink:href="data:image/jpeg;base64,{b64}"/></svg>')

# Light portrait — KenM.png
im = Image.open('/home/pop-os/Downloads/KenM.png').convert('RGB')
b64, n = to_jpeg_datauri(im)
svg = wrap_svg(b64, 1100, 1100)
open('public/images/profile-light.svg','w').write(svg)
print('profile-light.svg', os.path.getsize('public/images/profile-light.svg'), 'jpeg bytes:', n)

# Dark portrait — KenM-EDIT-EDIT.jpg
im = Image.open('/home/pop-os/Downloads/KenM-EDIT-EDIT.jpg').convert('RGB')
b64, n = to_jpeg_datauri(im)
svg = wrap_svg(b64, 1100, 1100)
open('public/images/profile-dark.svg','w').write(svg)
print('profile-dark.svg', os.path.getsize('public/images/profile-dark.svg'), 'jpeg bytes:', n)
EOF
